sources.entry: Siliconed - Open-source app for local AI image generation and instruction-based image editing on Apple silicon, written in Swift and Metal. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/gwenn-ha-dev/Siliconed) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.name: Siliconed
summary.one_liner: Siliconed is an open-source macOS app (Swift and Metal) that runs local AI image generation and instruction-based image editing on Apple silicon, offline, after benchmarking your Mac to choose the fastest kernels.
use_cases: generate images offline on a Mac
edit a photo with a text instruction
private AI art without cloud services
benchmark and tune image model speed on Apple silicon
finish a chosen image from an exploration grid
drive image generation from scripts or agents
summary.what_it_does: Siliconed runs five text-to-image and editing models (Krea 2 Turbo, Z-Image Turbo, Qwen-Image-2.1 Turbo, Anima Turbo, and beta MOSS-Image) locally on Apple silicon with no Python, server, or cloud. On first use after install or update, it benchmarks the Mac's GPU, CPU matrix unit (AMX), and Neural Engine, and enables only the kernels that verify correct and are measurably faster. Models run in full fp32 within a fixed memory budget, streaming weights from disk. It supports LoRAs, Civitai checkpoint import, instruction-based editing with one to three reference images, and a grid-based exploration mode. A command-line tool, silicontrol, controls the running app with JSON output.
notable: Per-Mac kernel benchmarking: enables GPU, AMX, and Neural Engine paths only when they verify and beat the default by at least 5%
Full fp32 renders checked against diffusers/transformers reference, with deterministic output for the same prompt, seed, settings and version
Half-size-grid early steps (Faster Rendering) for roughly a quarter to a third faster renders, with a switch to full-size recipe
Runs offline once a model is installed; weights pinned by revision and sha256
caveats: Requires macOS 26 or later and M1 or later Apple silicon

Model licenses differ: Krea 2 Community is commercial only under $1M annual revenue and requires a content filter when deployed; Qwen-Image-2.1 is non-commercial; Anima Turbo is non-commercial (images may be used commercially)
MOSS-Image support is beta and depends on a community 8-step LoRA
